implementation_notes: The modern JVM default: DefaultKafkaProducerFactory with a transactionIdPrefix hands out transactional producers, KafkaTemplate.executeInTransaction runs a block whose sends are staged until the template commits (and aborted if the block throws), and a TransactionTemplate or @Transactional method can wrap the same block; a database transaction joins the same unit of work only when the Kafka transaction manager is chained with the JDBC one. Choose this when Kafka is the boundary; choose XA only when one commit must genuinely span a database and the broker.
pitfalls: A @Transactional database method does not include the Kafka send: without chaining the Kafka transaction manager the two commits stay independent and the dual-write window returns.
executeInTransaction cannot be nested, and a send made through a different, non-transactional template inside the callback is not staged.
Transactional producers cost a coordinator round trip per transaction and the template must be configured before first use, so a lazily created template can silently fall back to plain sends.

variants.name: JTA/XA with a transactional JMS session
variants.implementation_notes: The classic JVM realization enlists the queue as a resource: a JMS Session opened in transacted mode (SESSION_TRANSACTED) or an XASession, plus an XADataSource for the database, and jakarta.transaction.UserTransaction (or the container) drives begin/commit across both, so the JDBC commit and the JMS send share one commit decision. The transaction manager owns the commit - Session.commit() must not be called on an enlisted session - and the price is two-phase commit, an in-doubt window and the need for XA-capable resources and a recovery log.
pitfalls: Never call Session.commit() on a session enlisted in a JTA transaction; the transaction manager owns the commit and a manual commit corrupts the branch.
XA requires XA-capable resources and a recovery log; a resource manager without proper recovery leaves in-doubt transactions after a crash.
Two-phase commit across a WAN or across services is an anti-pattern: keep XA inside one process, one transaction manager and one datacentre.
